title: Signed Proximity Matters in Graph-based Recommendation

problem.claim: Recommendation systems seek to leverage user-item interaction graphs for improved performance, including negative interactions such as dislikes and returns.

gap.claim: Unsigned graph models fail to exploit negative interactions, while existing signed-graph GNN approaches lack global information and Transformer approaches incur over-globalizing problems and substantial computational overhead.

contributions.claim: SPGNN upgrades GNN neighborhood aggregation with signed local proximity and signed global proximity based on weak balance theory to capture sign-aware multi-scale node relations.
SPGNN uses a theoretically grounded feature-initialization module that constructs sign-aware structure embeddings through fast spectral decomposition.
SPGNN is designed for top-K recommendation on signed graphs.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly distinguish two non-trivial technical contributions: signed local and global proximity notions, and a theoretically grounded feature-initialization module.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that SPGNN significantly outperforms unsigned and sign-aware models on six benchmark datasets.
The authors report gains of up to 19.42% in Recall and 28.18% in NDCG.
The authors report that code is available on GitHub.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph-based recommendation leverages user-item interaction structure.
Unsigned graphs omit negative interactions, motivating signed-graph recommendation.
Existing signed-graph GNNs lack global information, while Transformer approaches have over-globalizing behavior and high computational cost.
SPGNN combines signed local and global proximity with sign-aware spectral feature initialization.
Experiments on six benchmark datasets are reported to show improvements in Recall and NDCG.

source_observation.claim: The method combines local and global sign-aware graph relations in neighborhood aggregation.

interpretation.claim: Signed recommendation may benefit from modeling multi-scale relational structure rather than relying only on unsigned or purely local aggregation.

application.claim: For recommendation tasks with positive and negative interactions, consider separate sign-aware mechanisms for local and global proximity.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers to domains without signed interactions or beyond the reported benchmark setting.

source_observation.claim: The reported model uses fast spectral decomposition for sign-aware structure embeddings.

interpretation.claim: Structure-aware initialization may provide a computationally lighter way to incorporate global signed information than fully global architectures.

application.claim: When global structural information is useful but computational overhead is constrained, evaluate spectral structure embeddings as an initialization strategy.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the spectral method's scalability limits or initialization sensitivity.

unknowns: The six benchmark dataset names and their characteristics are unspecified.
The abstract does not describe the evaluation protocol, baselines, statistical variation, or ablation results.
The precise definitions of signed local proximity, signed global proximity, weak balance theory, and the spectral decomposition procedure are unspecified.
The computational overhead and scalability of SPGNN are not quantified.
The abstract does not report limitations or failure cases.
